title: Recruiting desk
_comment: Sourcing and screening for a hiring desk. CRM holds candidates; calendar books screens; email is the chase. Batch is how a longlist is screened without serial sandbox latency.

source_candidates.description: Given a role brief, find or import candidates into the CRM. Prefer reads; never invent people who do not exist in a connected source.

needs.description: What this run needs from the CLIENT before it can produce the work, in the client’s own words — one plain item per entry. Name the thing THEY would name: the document, the answer, the decision, the access. Populate this WHENEVER the run cannot finish because something only the client has is missing. Each entry becomes a request in their portal with an upload box; what they send is mounted into the next run’s ./inputs/, so an accurate ask here is what unblocks the work. Never use our nouns — a request naming a case, a schema or a connection id is unanswerable by the person receiving it. At most four, most important first. Leave absent when the work completed — an empty ask sent to a client is worse than silence.

input_schema._comment: A SWEEP over open roles, scheduled daily with an empty input — the blueprint's note says to look at open cases and, if there is no brief, say the desk is empty and never invent people. So nothing is required.

role.description: Narrow to one role. Absent means every open role on the desk.

brief.description: The role brief, when the caller already has it. Absent means read it from the case.

source_candidates._comment_client_facing: Builds the longlist. The written screen is what the client receives.

screen_candidate._comment_internal: One candidate, scored. A child of the batch; screen_longlist is what a client receives.
screen_candidate.description: Score one candidate against the role brief. Child of a batch when screening a longlist.

input_schema._comment: ONE candidate against ONE brief, usually a child of a longlist batch. Both are required: a score with no candidate is meaningless and a score with no brief is a guess wearing a number.

brief.description: What the role actually needs. REQUIRED — the bar has to come from somewhere the founder set.

screen_longlist.description: Fan out screen_candidate for each person on the longlist, then rank from the batch aggregate.

artifacts.description:
THE WORK ITSELF, not a description of it.

Every deliverable task in this system produced a summary and nothing else, and a client scored one 3/10 partly for that reason: they were sent an account of work rather than the work. A service business does not sell reports about bookkeeping, it sells reconciled books; it does not sell a note about a questionnaire, it sells the questionnaire answered.

So this carries the artifact. A file you wrote to ./output/ and its name, or a URL to something live, or a repository. The `client_summary` is the covering note that goes WITH this — it is not a substitute for it, and a deliverable with an empty `artifacts` array is a deliverable that did not deliver.

Say so plainly in the summary if you genuinely could not produce the artifact, and why. That is a real outcome. Pretending the summary is the work is not.

For this job: The longlist as a document, with each candidate's name, evidence and contact route — the thing the client reads and acts on, not a description of it.

kind.description: `file` for something you wrote to ./output/, `url` for something live, `repo` for source.

name.description: What it is, in the client's words. 'September ledger', not 'output.csv'.

path.description: Relative to ./output/ for a file. Required for kind=file.

what_it_is.description: One line the client reads before opening it.

no_candidates_to_screen.description: True when the longlist is empty or no candidate could be screened against the brief. Then leave `ranked` absent; an empty ranking reads as 'nobody was good enough', which is a different and untrue claim.

ship_checks._why: A ranking of nobody is worse than no ranking: the client reads a considered shortlist that does not exist.

The written screen per candidate is the product here — the landing page sells 'a longlist with a written screen on every candidate'. Five candidates sharing one paragraph is the single most visible way to prove nobody read them.

sections.heading: The read on this longlist
sections.must: Whether the role can be filled from these people, and the single thing most likely to stop it.

sections.heading: Ranked
sections.must: Every candidate in rank order with their score and the one line that decides their position. Rank order is the deliverable — an unordered list is the screening not done.

sections.heading: Why these, in order
sections.must: For the top of the list, what the evidence was. Cite the candidate's own record, never an impression.
sections.depth: a short paragraph each for the top few

sections.heading: Who we passed on, and why
sections.must: The rejections with the reason. A screen that only shows the winners cannot be checked.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.must: Who to talk to first, what to ask them, and what this desk needs to proceed.

input_schema._comment: Fans out one child per person, then ranks from the aggregate. The longlist is the work; without it this fans out nothing and then ranks it.

brief.description: The role brief, passed to every child so all of them score against the same bar.

intake_asks.ask: Role brief / scorecard for this search
Confirm the hiring manager and interview loop

workflows.name: workbook
workflows.description: Turn a grid you have already decided is correct into a real Excel workbook (.xlsx), attached to this delivery automatically. Use it for anything a client will sort, filter or forward — a longlist, a ranking table, a budget, a control matrix. Do NOT use it to do arithmetic: it formats what you give it and never re-totals a column.

currency.description: ISO-4217. Omit it and money renders as a plain number, which is honest.

tabs.description: One per sheet. A tab per schedule beats one sheet with blank rows between sections.

note.description: A caveat rendered above the header, for something that must be read before the numbers.

rows.description: Each row is an array of cells. A plain string or number is fine; for a formatted number use {kind:"n", v:1234, format:"money"|"pct"|"int"} and for a date {kind:"d", v:"2026-04-30"}.
